mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) signals sustained monetary accommodation that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point monthly increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals accelerating labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending power and corporate profit visibility, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises by >0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0%) indicates a weak economy with accommodative policy, triggering positive equity market reactions through expected policy support over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 7.0%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized) during early recovery phases signals robust aggregate demand, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: In early recovery phases, strong GDP growth (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signals manufacturing sector contraction, reducing corporate output capacity and profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS > 135,000) and real personal consumption (RSAFS > 420,000) signals strong consumer demand and labor market health, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through elevated corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 135000 and RSAFS > 420000, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Inflationary pressure (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized) erodes real corporate profits and triggers expectations of monetary tightening, driving negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through higher discount rates.
failure_condition: In inflationary pressure periods (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized), SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point monthly acceleration in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals imminent monetary policy tightening, reducing equity valuation multiples and driving negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by >0.5pp in 3 months.
